intro: To download a Canva design as a PDF on Mac, open the design and click Share in the top-right corner, then choose Download. In the panel, set File type to PDF Print for printing or PDF Standard for screens, then click Download at the bottom to save the file.
tldr: Open the design, click Share in the top-right corner, then choose Download.
Pick PDF Print for printing or PDF Standard for screens and email.
Tick crop marks and bleed only when a print shop asks for them.
If the download stalls, save the design and check canvastatus.com before you retry.

blocks.text: What you need before you download

You need a Canva account and a design open in the editor. You can work in a browser at canva.com or in the Canva desktop app for Mac. Save your design first, because an export can miss edits that have not saved yet. Your internet connection should be steady for the whole download.

Your plan matters for some options. Sources disagree about PDF Print on the free plan. WTTB says Canva Free includes PDF Print. DesignExporter says PDF Print, crop marks and bleed are Pro only, but it does not cite Canva. Open the Download panel on your own account to see what you get.
Download a Canva design as PDF on Mac, step by step

The download route is the same for most designs. The Share button sits in the top-right corner of the editor. The steps on this page give the menu path for each click. Canva can rename menu labels in a new release, so read the label on your screen if it differs.
PDF Print or PDF Standard: which to pick

PDF Print gives higher quality and suits printing. PDF Standard gives lower quality and suits sharing or online viewing. The WPS guide describes the two options this way. Use PDF Print when a printer will handle the file. Use PDF Standard for email, a website or a client review.

rows: One guide says Pro only, another says Free. Check your panel.
Good fallback when a multi-page design fails to export
blocks.caption: PDF Print and PDF Standard compared

blocks.text: A common mistake is sending a PDF Standard file to a print shop. Sharpness can suffer on print. Going the other way is harmless, but you get a bigger file than you need for screens.
Crop marks and bleed for print shops

Crop marks show the printer where to trim. Bleed extends the background past the trim line, so a small trim error does not leave a white edge. The Munro Agency guide ticks crop marks and bleed in the Download panel when you export for print. Turn them on only when a printer asks, because they add space around the page.

To see the bleed on screen, open File > View settings and turn on Show print bleed. The Munro guide says a dotted line then marks the bleed area. That guide does not say whether it covers the Mac app or the web app, so check the menu label on your screen first.
Flatten PDF, page ranges and file size

Flatten PDF fixes the layers in the exported file so they stop moving. Appuals notes that flattening can increase file size and makes layers static. Turn it on when the PDF shows blank areas, or when the option appears and your printer asks for it.

Page selection lives in the Download panel. Use it when a long design is slow or fails. Appuals suggests selecting half the pages and exporting that group, then splitting again if the export still fails. If each page works alone, export in batches and combine the PDFs afterward.
Download from the Canva desktop app on Mac

If you use the Mac app, open the design in your browser first. Click your profile icon and choose Open in desktop app. Lilach Bullock's guide says that opens Canva if the app is installed, or offers Download Canva for Mac if it is not. One Mac download covers both Apple and Intel chips, as of October 2026.

Keep the app current. The same guide says Canva may disable app versions older than six months, and sooner if a critical bug is found. An old build is the first suspect when exports misbehave. The guide also says most features work in the browser but does not cover PDF export, so test one page before you rely on the app for final files.
Why the Canva PDF download fails

Most failed downloads show one of a few symptoms. Appuals lists a download that stays on Preparing your download, a page stuck on Saving or Reconnecting, a Download limit reached message, and a Failed with Network Error message. The file can also come out blank or wrong.

items: Preparing your download never ends: check canvastatus.com, then try an incognito window.
Download limit reached: wait. The limit is rolling and resets after 24 hours. Clearing the browser does not help.
Blank or wrong PDF: try PDF Standard or PDF Print, turn on Flatten PDF, and turn off crop marks and bleed if you do not need them.
Multi-page design fails: export half the pages at a time to find the page that breaks.
One page fails: open that page alone, check Position > Layers for broken-media icons, delete the suspect element and retry.

blocks.text: Save and check status before you download

Start with File > Save in the editor. Wait for the confirmation before you click Share. Then check canvastatus.com for incidents, because a service problem can stop downloads for everyone. The Thatpainter guide makes the same first check, and it is the quickest test you can run.

If the editor will not load the design for download, go to the Canva home page. Open Recent designs or your folder, then click More and choose Download. Appuals describes the same fallback from the Projects view, so you can export without reopening the full editor.
Premium elements and watermarks

Thatpainter notes that people without Canva Pro can get a watermarked export when the design includes premium content. To test it, replace the premium elements and export again. If the watermark disappears, a premium asset caused it. Check the design for premium elements before you export a final file.
Keyboard shortcuts for this task

This page does not list a keyboard shortcut for the PDF download. None of the guides used for this page names a Canva shortcut for exports, so this page does not guess one. The steps use the mouse and the menus. If Canva adds a shortcut in a later release, check it on your own screen before you rely on it.
How many designs you can download at once

Free accounts have no native way to download several designs at once, according to DesignExporter. That third-party guide says Pro lets you download up to 200 designs in one ZIP file. This page could not check Canva's own help pages, so confirm the limit on your account before you plan a large batch.
Where the PDF lands on your Mac

Your browser saves the PDF to its download folder. For most people that is Downloads. Open the browser's download list to find the file. Browser settings vary, so if the file is missing, check the download location in the browser settings, then search for the file name in Finder.
Check the PDF before you send it

Open the PDF in Preview. Scroll every page, then check fonts, photos and the page count. Zoom in on small text and logos. If a photo is missing or blurry, go back to the design and fix that element before you download again.
Common mistakes to avoid

items: Sending a PDF Standard file to a print shop without asking first.
Turning on crop marks for a screen file, which adds space you do not need.
Downloading before the design saves, then missing your last edit.
Waiting on a download the browser has blocked. Check the download list first.
Trusting an old guide's menu names. The third-party guides on this page do not show a Canva version number.

blocks.text: Another mistake is skipping the preview step. A PDF that looks fine in the browser can still show a missing image after export. Open the file on your Mac and check it once before the design goes to a client or a printer.
Next steps after your first PDF

Once the PDF works, keep the same settings for the next design. If you have not set up the app yet, read [how to download and install the Canva desktop app on Mac](/how-to/download-and-install-canva-in-canva). If Canva alerts get in the way, read [how to turn on notifications in Canva on Mac](/how-to/turn-on-notifications-in-canva).

If the desktop app keeps failing, [reset it without losing designs](/how-to/reset-the-desktop-app-in-canva). Lilach Bullock's guide says the reset deletes Canva-related folders in your Library folder, but it does not delete designs. For role-specific routines, see [Canva for designers on Mac](/for/designers/canva) or [Canva for social media managers on Mac](/for/social-media-managers/canva).

faq.question: Is PDF Print free in Canva?
faq.answer: Sources disagree. WTTB says Canva Free includes PDF Print. DesignExporter says PDF Print, crop marks and bleed are Pro only. Open the Download panel on your own account to see what your plan shows.

faq.question: Why does my PDF come out blank?
faq.answer: Try PDF Standard or PDF Print, then turn on Flatten PDF. If the page still looks wrong, open that page alone and check Position > Layers for broken-media icons. Replace the broken element and retry.

faq.question: Can I download a Canva design as PDF from the web app instead of the Mac app?
faq.answer: Yes. The steps on this page start in the browser editor. No guide used here confirmed that the desktop app exports PDFs the same way, so test one page before you rely on it.

faq.question: Why does my download say Download limit reached?
faq.answer: Appuals says Canva uses a rolling 24-hour limit. Wait for the limit to reset. Clearing your browser data does not help.

faq.question: Do I need crop marks for a flyer I print at home?
faq.answer: Usually no. Crop marks help a print shop trim the sheet. A home printer does not need them, so leave them off for home printing.

faq.question: How do I check bleed before I send a PDF to print?
faq.answer: Open File > View settings and turn on Show print bleed, according to the Munro Agency guide. The guide says a dotted line marks the bleed area. Check the menu label on your screen first.

faq.question: Can I download many designs at once?
faq.answer: Free accounts have no native way to do that, according to DesignExporter. That guide says Pro lets you download up to 200 designs in one ZIP file. Confirm the limit on your account.

task: Download a Canva design as a PDF on Mac
appliesTo: Canva editor in a browser or the Canva desktop app on macOS
requirements: The design open in the Canva editor with edits saved
A Mac with a browser or the Canva desktop app
A steady internet connection for the whole download
A PDF viewer such as Preview

steps.name: Open the design
steps.text: Open the design in the Canva editor. You can use the browser at canva.com or the Canva desktop app for Mac. Wait until the page finishes loading before you export.
steps.tip: If the design will not open, try the home page and use Recent designs.

steps.name: Save and wait for the save to finish
steps.text: Open the File menu and choose Save. Wait for the confirmation before you go on. An export can miss edits that have not saved yet.
steps.tip: If Save does nothing, check canvastatus.com for an incident.

steps.name: Open the Share menu
steps.text: Click Share in the top-right corner of the editor. A menu opens with sharing and download options.
steps.tip: Share also handles invitations, so read the menu before you click.

steps.name: Choose Download
steps.text: In the Share menu, click Download. A panel opens with the file type and page options for the export.

steps.name: Set the file type
steps.text: Open the File type setting in the panel. Choose PDF Print for printing or PDF Standard for screens and email. PDF Print gives higher quality. PDF Standard gives a smaller file.
steps.tip: Some plans may not show PDF Print. Check the list on your own account.

steps.name: Tick crop marks and bleed if a printer asks
steps.text: For print jobs, tick Crop marks and Bleed in the same panel. Leave both off for screen files, because each one adds space around the page.
steps.tip: Ask the print shop whether they want bleed before you export.

steps.name: Turn on Flatten PDF if needed
steps.text: If the PDF looks wrong, or it shows blank areas, tick Flatten PDF when that option appears. Flattening can make the file bigger and makes layers static.
steps.tip: Flattening changes the exported file, not the design in Canva.

steps.name: Choose pages if the design is long
steps.text: For a multi-page design, use the page selection options in the panel to pick only the pages you need. Start with a few pages if the export fails.

steps.name: Click Download
steps.text: Click the Download button at the bottom of the panel. Your browser starts the file. Wait for the progress to finish before you close the tab.
steps.tip: If it stays on Preparing your download, see the troubleshooting list below.

steps.name: Check the PDF on your Mac
steps.text: Open the file from your browser's download list. Scroll every page, then check fonts, photos and the page count before you send it anywhere.
steps.tip: If your Mac does not open the file by default, open it in Preview.

troubleshooting.fix: Check canvastatus.com for an incident first. Then try an incognito window and turn off content blockers. For a large file, export PDF Standard or split the pages.

troubleshooting.problem: Browser shows Failed with Network Error
troubleshooting.fix: Check your connection, then retry. Turn off content blockers that may stop the download. Try another browser and look in the download list.
Wait. The limit is rolling and resets after 24 hours. Clearing your browser data does not help, according to Appuals.

troubleshooting.problem: PDF is blank or shows the wrong content
troubleshooting.fix: Choose PDF Standard or PDF Print, turn on Flatten PDF, and turn off crop marks and bleed if you do not need them. Flattening can increase the file size.
In Share > Download, select half the pages and export that group. Keep dividing to find the failing page. If each page works alone, export in batches and combine the PDFs.

troubleshooting.problem: One page fails or shows broken media
troubleshooting.fix: Open that page alone. Check Position > Layers for blank thumbnails or broken-media icons. Delete the suspect element and retry. Premium content without Pro can also add a watermark.
